spec_issues: The prompt forbids starting from a specialist IDM ('you may not start from p-doom/idm'). It is silent on training on that model's outputs. p-doom publishes 600 h of p-doom/idm pseudo-labels (p-doom/AGI-CAST-idm-actions) on the same macOS p(doom) screencast domain as the test clips. The review rule (tests/task/review.py:22-32) checks initialization only. Argon (1rmzib, 645e3z) and DeepSeek (4v1bcz) trained on these labels and passed. Opus (31drnp [14], 4qzbyj [13]) and Fable (5y7gp8 [18]) avoided them as forbidden. Argon 1rmzib is the $50 winner, so this unstated line decides a winner.

The held-out set is 43 of the 44 clips of the public, ungated HF dataset p-doom/idm-eval (tests/task/idm_sources.json; tests/task/idm_data.py:20-23 'all other clips ... are held out'), and also sits in the public inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks repo (tests/data.json). Only the prompt rule protects it. No trial downloaded it: every p-doom/idm-eval mention in the 18 trajectories is a metadata listing or the prompt text.

CONTRACT.md says 'Each scroll is labelled once, on the frame it happened'. The actual GT (tests/task/actions.py:45-110, 327) labels every 200 ms frame with nonzero scroll delta, after dropping keylog scroll runs. DeepSeek 50q2od discovered this by reading actions.py. The supplied actions.py lets agents work it out, so this is minor.
verifier_issues: Score = micro-F1 x 100 with no floor (raw metric already 0-1). Matching rules (tests/task/actions.py:133-136): MouseMove is exact-frame presence with details ignored, scroll is exact frame plus sign, keys and clicks need an exact string within -2..+3 frames. MouseMove frames are the largest action class, so cursor-motion detection dominates the score.
Only 43 clips (919 GT actions; e.g. Opus 4qzbyj tp 664 fp 108 fn 255). Clip-level sampling noise is a few F1 points, so the $50 gap between Argon 1rmzib (68.7) and Opus a7zigx (66.9) is within noise.
More than 5% failed clips scores zero (tests/task/validate.py:52,184). No trial hit it.
task_level.noise: Wallet ordering is non-monotone for most models: Opus 72.6/66.9/78.5, Fable 56.8/64.4/63.2, Argon 41.7/68.7/67.1, Muse 34.5/48.1/29.5, DeepSeek 40.0/39.5/43.3. Only Astra rises monotonically (44.9/55.9/67.2). Approach choice dominates wallet size: Opus's $10 synthetic-compositing run beats every non-Opus run at any wallet. The $50 winner (Argon 68.7 vs Opus 66.9) would flip under plausible 43-clip noise. $10 and $200 (Opus by 16 and 11 points) are robust.
task_level.elicitation: No harness effect is visible. Astra worked 0.9-1.3 h per trial and never fine-tuned a VLM. It shipped frozen Qwen3-VL plus small synthetic-trained cursor CNNs, with no imagegen or sub-agent use. Gemini runs are re-runs (-r2) from 10-13/14, after the source release. None touched the benchmark repo, the HF tasks dataset or frontierml.org (the only 'frontier-ml' hit is the local /opt/frontier-ml tool directory).
task_level.epoch_rationale: No review fails, no infrastructure zeros. The $50 winner (Argon 1rmzib 68.7) trained on pseudo-labels from the forbidden specialist p-doom/idm. That is allowed by the written rules and the reviewer, but read as forbidden by Opus and Fable. Under that reading Opus a7zigx (66.9) wins $50. The margin is also within noise.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Mostly real engineering, some of it inventive. The top runs got real or exactly-labelled data in the test format. Opus converted PSAI human Windows recordings to crowd-cast events and ran them through the official label extractor (a7zigx [25], 4qzbyj). Opus 31drnp composited scripted actions onto real AGI-CAST frames, scoring 72.6 for $5.63. Fable recorded its own Xvfb/XTest sessions. The other high-scoring family (Argon 68.7/67.1) is distillation of the forbidden specialist through its published pseudo-labels: legitimate under the letter of the rules, not under their evident intent. No trial touched idm-eval clips.
